plan.summary: Add optional iterative plan refinement behind --rounds, preserving byte-for-byte round-1 behavior and adding cost warnings, audit trail, and early-stop convergence.

steps.action: Implement a revision-capable round_table adapter in mirofish_lab/simulation.py so each implementer can revise from prior outputs rather than only contribute fresh content.
steps.observability: Adapter output shape, revision prompts, and parity of single-pass behavior when not used.

steps.action: Add regression tests for multi-round report rendering, early-stop convergence per persona, and round-1 golden parity.
steps.rollback: revert the new test cases and keep the prior regression suite
steps.observability: Golden diffs for rounds=1, convergence stop cases, and transcript completeness across rounds.

steps.action: Extend pre-flight-rehearsal/cli.py with --rounds N control flow that keeps the current single-pass path unchanged for N=1.
steps.rollback: revert to the prior single-pass CLI path
steps.observability: Byte-for-byte stdout/stderr parity for --rounds 1 and correct branching only when N>1.

steps.action: Add estimated cost warning output at CLI startup when --rounds > 1, including the expectation that extra rounds increase LLM calls.
steps.rollback: disable --rounds>1 and revert to default single-pass
steps.observability: Presence and wording of the warning, plus no warning for --rounds 1.

steps.action: Implement iterative refinement rounds in the CLI: after the initial parallel pass, run additional rounds where each persona sees the merged plan set, can revise, and stops early if two consecutive rounds are effectively identical for that persona.
steps.observability: Per-persona round counts, stop-trigger events, and unchanged single-pass semantics when N=1.

steps.action: Update report rendering to include per-round sections such as 'Plan: Minimalist (round 1)' and 'Plan: Minimalist (round 2)', plus explicit evolution visibility for the Judge input.
steps.rollback: Remove round-by-round transcript from reports and restore single-pass logs
steps.observability: Report section ordering, round labels, and audit trail completeness for every emitted round.

steps.action: Preserve the existing report schema and persisted artifacts exactly when --rounds 1, including judge payloads and output formatting.
steps.rollback: revert to the previous single-pass report generator
steps.observability: Golden diff checks on rendered reports and persisted artifacts for round-1 runs.

steps.action: Add round-aware storage only if needed for history/evolution tracking, keeping any schema changes within the maintenance window and with bounded backfill batches.
steps.rollback: drop the new storage objects and keep the old schema
steps.observability: Schema migration success, IOPS during backfill, and whether legacy columns remain intact.

steps.action: Brief support, assign an escalation owner, and publish release notes explaining the new multi-round behavior, cost warnings, and stopping rules.
steps.rollback: pause rollout until support briefing is complete
steps.observability: Support readiness signoff, named escalation owner, and release note publication status.

steps.action: Roll out the feature only outside incident windows, launch windows, and major events, with the new behavior staying behind the --rounds flag.
steps.rollback: pause rollout and hold at current version
steps.observability: Incident status, deploy freeze status, and whether the flag remains default-off.

steps.action: Enable customer-facing use of round-history reports only after customer notice and partner review approvals are satisfied.
steps.rollback: Revert to the prior report layout without round history
steps.observability: Customer notice timing, partner review approval, and whether externally shared reports include round evolution sections.

open_questions: What threshold should define 'effectively the same plan' for convergence detection?
Should the cost warning be a fixed message or include estimated dollar/token values?
Is round-aware storage actually required, or can round history live only in ephemeral reports and logs?
Who is the intended named escalation owner for customer support?

conflicts.issue: BackendOwner requires byte-for-byte identical round-1 behavior, while Security requires an audit trail for each round's inputs and outputs. Resolved by keeping round-1 unchanged and only adding round transcript visibility on the multi-round path.

ProductPM requires release notes and customer notice before externally visible report changes, while the CLI change can be implemented earlier. Resolved by staging code behind the flag and gating external exposure on comms approvals.

Round-history storage changes, if needed, must happen in a maintenance window, while CLI behavior can be rolled out outside incident windows. Resolved by separating code rollout from any storage migration and sequencing storage work only if required.
